fatal_errors: The proposed Ni-modified austenitic stainless steel is unrelated to the target NbMoTaW/NbMoTaWRe refractory high-entropy-alloy films.
It omits the target intervention of Re addition and 120 keV He implantation, as well as the irradiation-hardening and grain-boundary-embrittlement problem.
None of the cited evidence directly supports the claim that increasing Ni in austenitic stainless steel increases tensile ductility.
The assertion that Ni activates additional FCC slip systems is misleading: FCC already possesses its standard slip-system set, while Ni primarily affects phase stability and deformation mechanisms.
Allowing simultaneous Cr or Mo adjustments would confound the proposed Ni-concentration test.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses ductility only in a very broad sense and does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, irradiation conditions, defect-sink mechanism, or observed mechanical outcomes. The target concerns Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions suppressing helium-bubble growth and irradiation embrittlement in sputtered NbMoTaW-based films. The proposed stainless-steel mechanism and tensile outcome are therefore scientifically orthogonal. Its falsification experiment is reasonably testable, but it requires tighter compositional control and direct phase-stability measurements. The cited papers concern refractory HEAs, eutectic HEAs, B2/BCC phase decomposition, and Ni-based compositionally complex alloys; they do not validate the specific Ni–ductility claim.
